mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement 'X gives N to Y' appears, subtract N from X and add N to Y, updating each person's count accordingly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer (including gifts, donations, or any 'gives' phrasing) is encountered.
mathgap.example: Leaving Alice's count unchanged after 'Alice gives 3 cucumbers to Bob' and adding 3 to Bob.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a distinct variable for each person and translate every relevant statement (counts, differences, relational equations) into a linear equation relating those variables.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After all transfers have been applied and the current counts are known, for each remaining statement formulate an equation.
mathgap.example: Writing 'X has more than Y' as X - Y = N instead of treating it as two separate facts.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret any comparative phrasing that mentions a difference—such as 'X has more than Y', 'X has N more than Y', or 'the difference between X and Y'—as a signed difference X − Y, preserving the order given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a difference between two persons, convert it to an equation using X − Y.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has 5 more cucumbers than Y' as X − Y = 5, not as |X − Y| = 5.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements (including gifts, conditional transfers, splits, and redistributions) first, updating each person's count, and only then translate relational or difference statements into equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before setting up any equations, process every transfer-related sentence.
mathgap.example: Solving equations for differences before applying a prior transfer that changes the involved counts.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat statements that give an explicit count (e.g., 'X has N items') as the initial amount for X before any transfers or other operations are applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct count statement, record it as the starting value for that person.
mathgap.example: Reading 'Titus has 3 cucumbers' as setting Titus = 3 before any later redistribution.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: 'The final answer is \boxed{<integer>}' with no extra characters.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After computing the answer, before returning the response.
mathgap.example: Writing 'The final answer is \boxed{42}' instead of 'Answer: 42' or just '42'.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form 'If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y', first evaluate the condition using X's current count; if true, set X to 0 and add its previous amount to Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a conditional transfer sentence appears, after all prior transfers have been applied.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a conditional transfer without checking the condition, always moving X's items to Y.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The number of X increases by a/b times', interpret it as multiplying X's current count by (1 + a/b). For example, 'increase by 7/4 times' means new = old × 11/4.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever an 'increase by' phrase appears, apply the multiplicative factor to the current count of the mentioned person.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'increase by 2 times' as new = old × 2 instead of new = old × 3.

mathgap.title: Equal distribution handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form 'X and Y redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount', combine X and Y's current counts, compute the total, and set each to half of that total. For statements 'X splits all the items she owns equally among A and B', give each of A and B half of X's current count and set X's count to zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering any redistribution or split sentence, replace the involved persons' counts accordingly before solving equations.
mathgap.example: Leaving Ramona and Eduardo's counts unchanged after a redistribution statement, rather than setting each to (Ramona+Eduardo)/2.

mathgap.title: Swap handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X and Y switch the cucumbers they have' (or similar), exchange the entire counts of X and Y without altering the total sum.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a swap sentence appears, simply swap the variable values for the two persons.
mathgap.example: Adding Adrian's and Vivian's counts together instead of swapping them when the statement says they switch.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that an explicit count is the end state, ignoring later transfer or redistribution actions that modify the amount.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Record direct counts as initial values, then apply all subsequent transfer, split, and redistribution operations before using the counts in equations.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the giver and receiver, subtracting from the recipient and adding to the giver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a sentence says 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the order of the operands and treats 'X has N more than Y' as |X−Y|=N, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate any comparative difference phrase into a signed equation X − Y = N, preserving the order as stated.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by X times' as multiplying by X
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'increase by' is taken to mean a simple multiplication, ignoring that the increase is additive on top of the original amount.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Convert 'increase by a/b times' into a factor of (1 + a/b) and multiply the current count by that factor.

mathgap.description: Incorrect handling of equal distribution statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model either leaves the amounts unchanged or splits incorrectly, failing to combine totals and assign half to each participant.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For 'X and Y redistribute', set both to (X+Y)/2; for 'X splits all ... equally among A and B', set A and B each to X/2 and set X to 0.
